questions.q: The priority order of power is Inline > Embedded > External > Browser (Default). If all four style sources target the same element with different colors, which one wins?
options: Browser (Default)
External
Embedded
Inline

questions.q: In your stylesheet, an <h2> rule at the top sets color: blue, and another <h2> rule 100 lines later sets color: red. Both are plain element selectors (equal specificity). What color will the <h2> actually be?
options: Blue, because it was written first
Red, because when specificity is equal, the last rule in the file wins (the Cascade)
It will be a mix of blue and red
Neither -- the browser will show an error

questions.q:
A

tag has both class="highlight" and id="intro". One rule targets .highlight { color: blue; } and another targets #intro { color: red; }. What color wins, and why?
options: Blue, because class was written second
Red, because ID selectors have higher specificity than class selectors
Blue, because class selectors always beat ID selectors
It's a tie, so the browser picks black

questions.q: In HSL, what does a Saturation of 0% mean, regardless of what the Hue value is set to?
options: Full, vibrant color
The color will be some shade of gray (no color)
The color will be pure white only
Saturation has no visual effect

questions.q: Why should you always write a 'font stack' like font-family: "Roboto", "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif; instead of just one font name?
options: It makes the file load faster
It provides backup fonts in case the first choice fails to load, ending in a safe generic family
Browsers require at least 4 font names to work
It's only for decoration, it has no real function

questions.q: Why do professionals prefer rem units over fixed px units for font sizing?
options: rem is relative to the root <html> element's font size, so text scales properly if a user changes their browser's accessibility font settings; px stays fixed no matter what
px and rem are exactly the same, it's just a style preference
rem only works on mobile devices
px automatically adjusts for screen size while rem does not

ch6_lab_boxmodel.title: Quick Check: Box Model, Reset & Pseudo-Classes

questions.q: Without box-sizing: border-box, if you add 20px of padding to an element with width: 100px, what happens to its total rendered width?
options: It stays exactly 100px
It grows to 140px, because padding is added on top of the declared width
It shrinks to 80px
The browser throws an error

questions.q: Why do professionals add a Universal Reset (the * selector setting margin: 0; padding: 0;) at the top of their stylesheet?
options: To make the page load faster
To strip away each browser's own default margins/padding so the site looks consistent instead of slightly different on Chrome vs Safari vs Edge
It's required for CSS to work at all
To disable all CSS on the page

questions.q: What is the key difference between a pseudo-class like :hover and a pseudo-element like ::before?
options: They are identical, just different spellings
A pseudo-class (one colon) targets a special state of an element; a pseudo-element (two colons) targets a specific part of an element or generates new phantom content
Pseudo-elements only work on links
Pseudo-classes require JavaScript to function
